diffs.diff: chip ID register 0xc: part 34305, datasheet reading 390
diffs.evidence: Vishay VCNL4040 datasheet (doc 84274) Table 13: 'ID_L 0CH_L (0CH data byte low) 86H ... device ID LSB byte'; 'ID_M 0CH_H ... Version code (0:0:0:1), device ID MSB byte' (register table: ID_L 0x86, ID_M 0x01), and the read protocol returns 'Data byte low' then 'Data byte high'. So the chip ID is 0x0186 = 390, transmitted as bytes 0x86, 0x01. The second reading's 390 is the logical value. The model's sim register 34305 = 0x8601 is the same ID written in wire byte order, because the simulator's 16-bit registers (src/sim/devices.ts setReg) send the high byte first. The driver assembles d[0] | d[1]<<8 and checks ident == 0x0186, and SKILL.md documents ID = 0x0186, both matching the datasheet. check.ts PASSes with the driver reading 0x0186 from the sim. Storing 390 would make the sim send 0x01,0x86 and the driver would read 0x8601 and fail.
